disputes.reason: Ambiguous: a change in a firm's risk appetite can itself prompt reassessment of third-party contracts, so a candidate could argue the statement is true; 'is an event' is a category quibble, not a clear fact.

Not clearly false: MiFID II (the MiFID II/MiFIR regime) contains whistleblowing/reporting-of-infringements provisions (e.g. Art. 73), so a candidate can reasonably argue whistleblower protection is addressed by the regime; the card only holds under a narrow reading of MiFIR alone.

Multi-claim, number-heavy card (largest penalty, USD 11 bn buy-back + USD 150 m penalties, ARS misrepresentation) whose figures and 'July 2008' dating do not match the public record (UBS ARS settlement was August 2008 with a buy-back of roughly USD 18-19 bn); cannot be confirmed as a safe fact for a student.

Swapped-numbers card that relies on the same unverifiable USD 11 bn / USD 150 m split, which conflicts with the public record of the UBS ARS settlement; tests memory of a doubtful figure rather than a syllabus principle.
